drivingQuestion: Do Rav and Rav Asi disagree over whether to accept Rav Ḥisda's rule about a robbed item consumed by another, or over whether gifts of the priesthood can be stolen?
outcomeNote: The proposal that the dispute turns on Rav Ḥisda is rejected; the dispute is relocated to whether priestly gifts can be stolen, and a variant version teaches that dispute on its own.

segments.he: לֵימָא בִּדְרַב חִסְדָּא קָא מִיפַּלְגִי, דְּאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: גָּזַל וְלֹא נִתְיָיאֲשׁוּ הַבְּעָלִים, וּבָא אַחֵר וַאֲכָלוֹ – רָצָה מִזֶּה גּוֹבֶה, רָצָה מִזֶּה גּוֹבֶה. דְּמָר אִית לֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא, וּמָר לֵית לֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא.
segments.en: The Gemara suggests: «Let us say» that «they disagree with regard to» a statement «of Rav Ḥisda, as Rav Ḥisda said:» In a case where one «robbed» another of an item, «and the owners had not despaired of retrieving» it, «and another» person «came and consumed» the stolen item, if the owner «wants, he» may «collect» the value of the stolen item «from this one,» the robber, and if he «wants, he» may «collect from that one» who consumed it. The suggestion is «that» one «Sage,» Rav, «holds» in accordance with the opinion «of Rav Ḥisda,» and he therefore holds that the priest may claim the maw from either the buyer or the butcher; «and» one «Sage,» Rav Asi, «does not hold» in accordance with the opinion «of Rav Ḥisda,» and the priest may therefore claim the maw from the buyer alone.

segments.he: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא, וְהָכָא בְּמַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה נִגְזָלוֹת קָא מִיפַּלְגִי, דְּמָר סָבַר נִגְזָלוֹת, וּמַר סָבַר אֵין נִגְזָלוֹת.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects this suggestion: «No; everyone holds» in accordance with the opinion «of Rav Ḥisda, and here they disagree with regard to» whether or not «gifts of the priesthood can be stolen. As» one «Sage,» Rav, «holds» that they «can be stolen,» and accordingly the robber remains responsible for them even if they are consumed by another. Consequently, if the butcher weighed the innards, the priest may claim the gifts from either the butcher or the buyer. «And» one «Sage,» Rav Asi, «holds» that gifts of the priesthood «cannot be stolen.» Since technically one cannot steal the gifts, the obligation to return them to the priest rests solely on the one in physical possession of them. Accordingly, the priest may claim the gifts from the buyer alone, as the gifts are in his custody.

segments.he: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ: רַב אָמַר: מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה נִגְזָלוֹת, וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה אֵין נִגְזָלוֹת.
segments.en: The Gemara notes that «some teach this halakha,» that there is a dispute between Rav and Rav Asi as to whether or not gifts of the priesthood can be stolen, «by itself,» i.e., as an independent dispute between them rather than in explanation of another dispute: «Rav says» that «gifts of the priesthood can be stolen, and Rav Asi says» that «gifts of the priesthood cannot be stolen.»

moves.summary: Suggests that Rav and Rav Asi disagree over whether they accept Rav Ḥisda's ruling.
moves.about: brings Rav Ḥisda's ruling that where one robbed and another consumed, the owner may collect from either party

moves.summary: Cites Rav Ḥisda: the owner of a stolen and consumed item may collect from either the robber or the consumer.
moves.about: the floated suggestion — later rejected — that Rav accepts Rav Ḥisda's rule that the owner may collect from either the robber or the consumer, and therefore lets the priest claim the maw from the butcher too

moves.cueHe: דמר אית ליה דרב חסדא, ומר לית ליה דרב חסדא
moves.summary: Spells out the suggestion: Rav accepts Rav Ḥisda and Rav Asi does not.
moves.about: the floated suggestion — later rejected — that Rav Asi does not accept Rav Ḥisda's rule that the owner may collect the value of a stolen item from whichever of the two he wishes

moves.cueHe: לא, דכולי עלמא אית להו דרב חסדא
moves.summary: Rejects the suggestion: everyone accepts Rav Ḥisda's ruling.
moves.about: rejects its own suggestion that the dispute turns on accepting Rav Ḥisda — everyone accepts him

moves.cueHe: והכא במתנות כהונה נגזלות קא מיפלגי
moves.summary: Relocates the dispute: they differ over whether gifts of the priesthood can be stolen.
moves.about: attributes to Rav the view that gifts of the priesthood can be stolen, so the robber remains liable even after another consumed them

moves.cueHe: איכא דמתני לה להא שמעתא בפני עצמה
moves.summary: Notes that some teach the dispute over stealing priestly gifts as an independent dispute, not as an explanation of another one.
moves.about: a second version in which Rav's ruling that priestly gifts can be stolen is taught as a free-standing statement rather than as the ground of the earlier dispute
